figures.caption: The first side is stopped at the east corner. The next source instruction prepares the south heading but has not executed.
figures.alt: Four annotated details at east stopped. The next instruction loads 180 into t1. The native tool reports position sixteen zero, heading ninety degrees, pen down and stopped, with sixty-four instructions per tick. Register t2 equals the target s1, both sixteen. An enlarged original board crop shows the first horizontal stroke and the right-pointing marker.

figures.caption: The second side is stopped at the lower-right corner. The heading and the coordinate being polled changed between the two legs.
figures.alt: Four annotated details at south stopped. The next instruction loads 270 into t1. The native tool reports position sixteen sixteen, heading 180 degrees, pen down and stopped, at sixty-four instructions per tick. Register t2 and target s1 both equal sixteen. An enlarged original board crop shows the rightward then downward pen trail and a downward-pointing marker.

figures.caption: The square is complete before the exit syscall. Returning to the origin and raising the pen are separate parts of the result.
figures.alt: Three annotated details at finished. The next source instruction selects exit service ten. The native tool reports position zero zero, heading zero degrees, pen up and stopped, with sixty-four instructions per tick. An enlarged original crop shows the retained closed square and upward-pointing position marker at the origin.

figures.caption: One native Backstep Instruction action restores the state before the first movement-stop store. The Debug session is still paused.
figures.alt: Four annotated details after actual Backstep Instruction from east stopped to east stop. The blue next instruction is the store of zero to movement offset fifty hexadecimal. The later breakpoint remains at the next heading load. The native tool reports position sixteen zero, heading ninety degrees, pen down and moving. Registers still contain feedback and target sixteen, and the enlarged board crop retains the first side.
